review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read initialForwardChart and initialForwardChart_zero in InitialForwardChart.lean, and mappedFutureArc_of_ne_zero in MappedFutureSimple.lean. I grepped all downstream uses of mappedFutureArc and initialForwardChart. I did not run Lean. Whether the proposed lemmas would work as simp lemmas, with the side condition discharged automatically, is unverified. The two findings are about missing nonzero-case rewrite lemmas for definitions that already have a zero-case simp lemma.

findings.problem: mappedFutureArc is an if-then-else on `(u:ℝ)=0`, and this file gives only its zero case as a simp lemma. The nonzero case, `mappedFutureArc … u = mappedFutureRaw … u` for `u ≠ 0`, is not provided here. It is proved later, in MappedFutureSimple.lean, as `mappedFutureArc_of_ne_zero`, which is not tagged simp and is not available in this file. So `mappedFutureArc_upper` (lines 91–99) unfolds the definition by hand with `change (if (u:ℝ)=0 then _ else _)∈upperHalfPlane` and `rw [ite_eq_right hc]`, and `mappedFutureArc_zero` does the same with `change` plus `ite_eq_left rfl`. Downstream files also use `change … mappedFutureArc … 0 - _ = 0` (CenteredFutureSlit.lean) and `change ‖mappedFutureArc … u - _‖ < ε` (FutureSlitRadius.lean) before rewriting. The simp interface covers only half the case split, and callers must unfold the if by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Move `mappedFutureArc_of_ne_zero` into this file, directly after `mappedFutureArc_zero`, and use it in `mappedFutureArc_upper`. Either tag it `@[simp]` or give it a `(u:ℝ) ≠ 0` side condition, so simp can discharge `u ≠ 0` from context. Also consider a lemma stating the `u ≠ 0` case with `(u:ℝ) ≠ 0` as the hypothesis, since the if-condition is stated on the real coercion.
findings.benefit: The lemma that unfolds the definition sits next to the definition. `mappedFutureArc_upper` no longer needs `change` and `ite_eq_right`. Downstream proofs can drop their `change` and `rw` boilerplate, because the zero and nonzero cases are both covered by named rewrites.

evidence.excerpt: mappedFutureArc p hi h0 hH hst ht u=mappedFutureRaw p hi h0 hH s t u := by

findings.problem: initialForwardChart is defined as `if ht : t=0 then id else (initialSlitChart …).forward`. It has a simp lemma only for `t = 0` (`initialForwardChart_zero`). For `s ≠ 0` there is no rewrite lemma. This line therefore unfolds the definition and strips the dite with `rw [initialForwardChart,dite_eq_right hs]`. The same two-step unfolding is repeated in at least eight other places: MovingForwardBoundaryHeight, InitialLimitInverse, InitialForwardComparison, InitialForwardChart, InitialChartIdentities, and InitialChartNormalization (three times). The pattern also appears for `initialCapacity` and `initialInverseChart`. Each call site exposes the dite implementation detail instead of using a canonical `initialForwardChart … s = (initialSlitChart … s hs).forward` normal form.
findings.proposed_change: In InitialForwardChart.lean, next to `initialForwardChart_zero`, add `lemma initialForwardChart_of_ne_zero … (hs : s ≠ 0) : initialForwardChart p hi h0 hH s = (initialSlitChart p hi h0 hH s hs).forward := dif_neg hs`. Use it here as `rw [initialForwardChart_of_ne_zero _ _ _ _ _ hs]`. Optionally tag it `@[simp]` and rely on `hs` in context. Do the same for `initialCapacity` and `initialInverseChart`.
findings.benefit: The simp interface covers both branches of the case split. Call sites stop depending on the dite-based definition, and their proofs become shorter and more robust if the definition changes.

evidence.excerpt: if ht : t=0 then id else (initialSlitChart p hi h0 hH t ht).forward
